title: Daily Bread
subtitle: Thirty days with God. Everything else in this program stands on it.
note: Week 4 runs nine days (22-30), not seven. Do NOT compute week from day for this course - use each day's own week_number.

week_list.title: Show Up
week_list.opening_line: This is the easiest week of your life and roughly half of women do not finish it.
week_list.stakes: Skip it and you spend the next three weeks reciting a practice you never actually built — and you will not find out until day twenty-four, which is the worst possible day to find out.
week_list.pull_quote: You are not building a devotional habit. You are finding out whether you actually believe anyone is listening, and you already suspect you don't.

blocks.v: The five things

items.head: Invite the Spirit
items.sub: Out loud, before anything else. Not a mood. An invitation, spoken.

items.head: Play one worship song
items.sub: From YouTube, out loud in the room, not buried in your earbuds. Let your body respond to it before your mind does.

items.head: Read the Scripture
items.sub: Slowly, twice. Once for the words, once for what they are actually asking of you.

items.head: Journal
items.sub: Answer the day's question, in your own handwriting, before you talk yourself out of the honest version.

items.head: Set your intention and hand it over
items.sub: Name what you are placing in His hands today. Then get up and go live the day.

blocks.v: Five minutes on a fast day. Twenty on a slow one. Nothing gets added to it for thirty days. On the day everything else falls apart, you still do this.

blocks.title: The five things, and where they go next
rows: Invitation
In every program after this one, the room opens the same way — you just won't be the only one saying it.
Worship
In Still Waters this becomes the whole practice, extended past one song into real stillness.
Scripture
In The Honest Room, Scripture is what steadies a woman while she looks at something true about herself.
Intention
In Strong and Surrendered, this is the same motion applied to your body instead of your day — asking, then not white-knuckling the outcome.

blocks.v: Falling is routine
Read this now, while nothing has gone wrong. You will miss a day. Probably several. The father in the story did not ask for the speech — he was already calling for the robe.

left.head: What you will make it mean
items: I can't even keep a five-minute practice.
I'm not the kind of woman who follows through with God either.
I'll start again on the first of the month.

right.head: What it actually is
items: Grace was already running toward me before I got back.
I moved the slot to the morning.

items.head: Mark the day honestly
items.sub: Do not skip it quietly. A blank is honest and a hidden blank is not.

items.head: Say four words
items.sub: "Missed one. Back today." No paragraph of reasons — the reasons are where the shame gets a foothold.

items.head: Do the five things anyway
items.sub: Right there, in whatever you are wearing. This is not a smaller version of the practice. It is the practice.

items.head: Go the next morning, ordinary
items.sub: The same five things, at your time, as though nothing happened — because as far as He's concerned, nothing did.

items.head: Invite, out loud, daily
items.sub: Every single day, before the song and before the page. Not thought. Spoken.

items.head: Worship, one song
items.sub: Played all the way through, before you ask for anything.

items.head: Scripture read twice
items.sub: Slowly. Once for the words, once for what they ask of you.

items.head: One time of day, kept
items.sub: The same slot, seven days running. This is the week's real assignment and it is not the praying.

blocks.title: The inner work — What You've Actually Asked For

items.head: Ten minutes, on paper
items.sub: Every prayer you can remember praying about your life in the last five years. All of them. Do not think, list.

items.head: Beside each one
items.sub: What happened. Answered, unanswered, or you honestly forgot you'd asked.

items.head: Circle the one you prayed the longest
items.sub: Not the biggest one. The one you kept bringing back.

items.head: One line underneath
items.sub: What made you stop bringing it back. Where you were standing when you quietly gave up asking.

blocks.text: Be still, and know that I am God.
blocks.why: Not a suggestion to relax. A command to stop performing long enough to notice who you are talking to.

blocks.title: Done means
items: Seven days shown up, seven of seven
The invitation spoken out loud all seven days
A time of day written down and kept at least five of the seven
The prayers page written in one sitting, with an outcome beside every line
Day seven's log read back in one sitting
blocks.demo: Say your time of day out loud, and say what you asked God for on day four, without opening the app.

blocks.q: Do you have a time of day, or a vague intention?
blocks.right: Six-forty, and I have kept it

blocks.q: Did you say the invitation out loud, or only think it?

blocks.title: When it doesn't work
rows: You did not pick a time of day
This is the corner, and it is the only one that matters this week. Everything downstream fails here. Pick one now, out loud, and write it in ink.
You prayed silently instead of out loud
Silent is not the same practice. Say it with your mouth. Something changes when the words leave your body and you will not believe it until you do it.
You skipped the worship song because you were in a hurry
The song is not decoration before the "real" prayer. It is what softens you enough to mean the rest of it. Do not cut it.
You are already bored
Good. Boring is what daily looks like from the inside, and the fact that you expected it to feel like something every time is the exact belief this month is dismantling.
You are ill, traveling, or overwhelmed
The five things become one line each. Log it as that. It counts identically and nobody is grading the content.

blocks.title: Not every hard thing is a corner to drill at
blocks.v: If the prayers page brought up something bigger than a habit — old material arriving with your whole body attached — that is not a corner and I will not treat it as one. Keep the daily practice and take that to somebody licensed to hold it.

week_list.title: Keep It
week_list.opening_line: Week two is where you meet the voice that has ended every good habit you have ever started with God, and it will not sound like an enemy. It will sound extremely reasonable.
week_list.stakes: Skip the negotiation and you will believe, for another decade, that you are a woman who cannot keep a promise to God — when what you actually are is a woman who has never once heard the sentence out loud.
week_list.pull_quote: You are not lazy and you are not spiritually shallow. You have been having a negotiation every morning that you did not know was happening.

blocks.v: The same five things, the same time, stays exactly as it was. The base does not change. What you notice about your resistance to it does.

items.head: Same five things, same time
items.sub: The base does not change. What goes on top is your attention to it.

items.head: Catch the negotiation
items.sub: The sentence your mind gives you for skipping today. Write it down, verbatim, the moment it arrives.

items.head: Read Scripture even on the dry day
items.sub: The day it feels like nothing. Especially that day.

items.head: The intention, said with your eyes open
items.sub: Once this week, don't close your eyes to release it. Say it looking at the room you're actually standing in.

items.head: Catch it in the act
items.sub: The morning it happens, stop and write the sentence down verbatim, in the voice it arrives in. Quotation marks.

items.head: Do not argue with it
items.sub: Not on paper, not in your head. You are collecting, not debating.

items.head: Collect three of them
items.sub: Over the week. Most women find the same one three times.

items.head: Read them back on day fourteen
items.sub: Out loud, standing, flat. That is the whole intervention and it works better than willpower.

blocks.title: Performing steadfastness, and actually keeping it

left.head: Performing it
items: Praying longer when you feel guilty
Skipping the hard day and calling it rest
Reading the verse without reading it twice
Writing what you think a "good" answer looks like

right.head: Keeping it
items: The same five minutes, every day, dry or not
Showing up especially on the day you'd rather not
Reading it twice even when nothing new comes
Writing the actual sentence, even the ungrateful one

blocks.text: Trust in the LORD with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding. In all thy ways acknowledge him, and he shall direct thy paths.
blocks.why: Not a feeling. A decision, made daily, in all your ways — including the boring ones.

blocks.title: Done means
items: Three negotiation sentences collected in quotation marks
The same time of day kept, or honestly logged when it moved
One dry-day Scripture read without a feeling attached, and named as such
The intention said once with your eyes open, in the room
Fourteen days shown up, fourteen of fourteen
blocks.demo: Read your three negotiation sentences out loud, flat, standing, without laughing at the end of any of them.

blocks.right: Word for word, its own voice

blocks.q: Did the time of day hold under pressure?
blocks.right: It held on the two hard days

blocks.title: When it doesn't work
rows: The negotiation never showed up in words
It is there and it is preverbal. Write what you did instead — the phone, the extra coffee, the reorganized morning. The behavior is the sentence.
You are logging but not writing
The written line is half the practice. Sixty seconds. Do not upgrade it into a journaling session, just answer the question.
You missed a day
Four words, the five things, the ordinary next morning. That is the entire protocol.
You are treating the invitation like a formality now
It got automatic before it got honest. Slow down and mean the words again, even if it takes longer than usual today.
The negotiation turned out to be about something much bigger than a quiet time
Very common in week two, and it is real. Keep the practice. Take the rest of it somewhere it can be properly held.

week_list.title: The Week You Miss
week_list.opening_line: I scheduled this week a year ago. If you have already missed a day, you are on time.
week_list.stakes: Skip this and the first missed day of the rest of your life ends the practice — because you will still be carrying a private rule that says a broken practice is a verdict on your faith, and you will never once have tested whether that's actually true.
week_list.pull_quote: Falling is not the interruption to walking with God. For most of us, it is most of the walking.

blocks.title: Return time is the only number that matters
blocks.v: Not the length of the streak. Not the total days. The gap, in days, between missing and coming back. A woman with a return time of one day will still be walking with God in ten years. A woman with a perfect record and no return plan is one bad Wednesday from stopping altogether, and she has no idea.

blocks.label: One long exhale
blocks.cue: Before you begin, let your shoulders actually drop. The difference between arriving braced and arriving open. Daily this week.

blocks.title: The two things a missed day can be

left.head: A verdict
items: I'm not the kind of woman who follows through with God either.
I'll start again on the first of the month.

right.head: Grace
items: He was already glad I came back.
The pattern is Wednesdays — I'll move the slot.

items.head: One long exhale before you begin, daily
items.sub: Let your shoulders actually drop before you speak. The difference between arriving braced and arriving open.

items.head: The five things, unchanged
items.sub: Same time. Non-negotiable, and this is the week that phrase gets tested.

items.head: One day with no requests, only listening
items.sub: Skip asking for anything. Read the Scripture, then sit in silence for a full minute before you write.

items.head: Practice the return, on purpose
items.sub: If nothing has gone wrong yet, miss on purpose one day this week and run the return protocol, so it is not the first time you've done it for real.

blocks.title: The inner work — The Return Plan

items.head: Write the four words now
items.sub: "Missed one. Back today." In the book, before you need it.

items.head: Name the likely day
items.sub: Look at your fourteen days. Which weekday is thinnest? That is the one coming for you.

items.head: Write what you will do at eleven at night
items.sub: Specifically. Which of the five things, in what room, in what clothes.

items.head: Write who you will tell
items.sub: One name, or the Circle. A return that nobody sees is one you can quietly cancel.

blocks.text: And he arose, and came to his father. But when he was yet a great way off, his father saw him, and had compassion, and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him.
blocks.why: The father was watching for him before he ever turned around.

blocks.title: Done means
items: The return plan written in full before day nineteen, all four steps
One day taken with no requests, only listening, and what surfaced named
Any miss logged as a blank, four words said, and the return time written as a number
Twenty-one days honestly accounted for — no invented entries
blocks.demo: Say your return plan out loud from memory: the four words, the room, the clothes, and the name of the person you tell.

blocks.q: What do you do at eleven at night on a missed day?
blocks.left: Bed, and quietly decide to restart Monday
blocks.right: The five things, four words, bed

blocks.q: Is your return plan written or intended?

blocks.title: When it doesn't work
rows: You have not missed a day and you are treating that as the achievement
The unbroken record is not the point. Write the return plan anyway, this week, while it is cheap. You are buying the insurance before the fire.
You fell and disappeared for four days
The falling was ordinary. The four days were the injury. Go back today, four words, no reason. Then write down what happened on day two that made day three easier to skip.
You posted the four words with a paragraph of explanation attached
The reason is where the shame gets in, and a paragraph is an invitation to be forgiven for something that was never a crime. Four words. That is the whole discipline.
The no-requests day made you anxious with nothing to hold onto
That is the week working. Sit in it once more before Sunday and say nothing about it to anybody yet.
What surfaced during the listening day was old and arrived with your whole body attached
That is not a lapse in discipline and it does not get drilled at. Keep the practice. Take that part to a licensed professional.

week_list.title: Nine Days
week_list.opening_line: Nine days, not seven. You are past the part where this is new and into the part where it is simply what you do.
week_list.stakes: Skip these last nine and you will have spent a month proving you can show up to God, and then quietly stop asking Him for anything — which is the specific way most women lose the second half of this practice.
week_list.pull_quote: Ask boldly. Prepare like it is coming. Then receive it without putting it down and running.

blocks.v: He gave a portion sized for one day, on purpose, and the asking is meant to happen again tomorrow. This is the week you say what you want out loud and let it be seen that you asked.

blocks.label: Standing to ask
blocks.cue: The ask is prayed out loud, standing, eyes open. Named and specific — not a private wish you never actually said.

items.head: The five things, nine of nine
items.sub: Nothing added and nothing skipped, including on the day nothing feels like happening.

items.head: Ask specifically, out loud, once
items.sub: Not a vague hope. A named thing, spoken with your eyes open.

items.head: Prepare like it's coming
items.sub: Do one small, real thing this week that only makes sense if the answer is yes.

items.head: One longer time with Him
items.sub: A full hour this week instead of the usual five minutes — a real walk if that's what you have, praying the whole way, or an hour at the table with the book open.

items.head: Ten minutes, verbs only
items.sub: What do you want God to do. Not a feeling, not a description of a better life. A verb. No ranking and no crossing out.

items.head: Circle the one that tightened your chest
items.sub: Not the sensible one.

items.head: Write what receiving it would actually require of you
items.sub: Four lines, no more. What you'd have to do, not just feel.

items.head: Pray it out loud, once, standing, eyes open
items.sub: Named, specific. God is for you and He is not vague. Neither should you be.

blocks.text: Every good gift and every perfect gift is from above, and cometh down from the Father of lights.
blocks.why: Ask boldly because of who you're asking, not because of how well you've performed the month.

blocks.title: Done means
items: Nine days shown up, nine of nine
One real thing posted in the Circle, in your own words, not the tidy version
One thing prepared for as though the answer is coming
The ask written, all four steps, and said out loud standing
Thirty days honestly accounted for by day thirty
blocks.demo: Say the thing you are asking God for out loud, in one sentence, with no preamble and no joke on the end.

blocks.q: Can you name what you're asking for as a specific thing, not a feeling?
Did you post the real version or the tidy one?
blocks.right: Posted the thin one. Left it up

blocks.v: Which door
You have the thirty days. That is the gate on all three programs and you are through it. Choose while it is still fresh.

blocks.title: The three doors
rows: You want your body brought into this the same way your mornings just were — asking, preparing, receiving, without white-knuckling the outcome
Strong and Surrendered. Eight weeks. The same surrender applied to your body.
You want to stay in this stillness and go deeper into it, not add anything to it
Still Waters. Four weeks. Christian contemplative practice with a real progression under it.
You did the therapy, you can name the pattern in one clean sentence, and you're ready to bring it into the light with other women watching
The Honest Room. Ten weeks, twelve seats, application required, and completed clinical work is a hard prerequisite alongside the thirty days.
You are not ready to choose
Stay in the app. The count does not reset, the Circle stays, and the door is open whenever you want it.
You want to do it again
Do it again. Nobody finds a second thirty days embarrassing. Second time through, take the asking more seriously and keep the same time of day.

blocks.title: When it doesn't work
rows: You cannot name a specific ask, only a feeling
Ask it differently. What would be different in your actual week if this were answered? Concrete first, the feeling comes free.
You posted the tidy version
Everybody does, the first time. Post one more, today, and make it the thinnest day you've had this month. Nobody will react the way you're afraid they will.
You didn't prepare because you're afraid the answer is no
Prepare anyway, in something small. Preparing is not presuming — it's what asking boldly looks like with your hands.
You are on day twenty-eight and quietly finished
This is the corner this week exists for. Two more. Ordinary ones. That is the entire remaining assignment.
